subject: Probabilities that mortality rates are greater than a given threshold value

messages.author: 8e04d3c51038d0ad
messages.subject: Probabilities that mortality rates are greater than a given threshold value
parts:
Hi INLA team,

I run the model through the code:

formula <- OBS_I ~1+
  f(RegionID, model='besagproper2', graph = H, constr=TRUE)+
  f(RegionID1, model='besagproper2', graph = H, group=TP1, control.group=list(model='iid'))+
  f(RegionID2, model='besagproper2', graph = H, group=TP2, control.group=list(model='iid'))+
  f(RegionID3, model='besagproper2', graph = H, group=TP3, control.group=list(model='iid'))+
  TP+instability+deprivation+dependency


model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN<-inla(formula, family="poisson", data=data ,E=EXP_I,
                         
                         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,quantiles = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)),
                         
                         control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE,waic=TRUE,config=TRUE),
                         
                         control.inla=list(strategy="simplified.laplace"))


The results are nice and satisfying. I calculated Relative risks then thorough below formula for 4 different time periods:

RR_period1   <- data.frame(RR1Mode=exp(TimePeriod1+S1.S+U.S))
RR_ period 2 <- data.frame(RR2Mode=exp(TimePeriod2+S2.S+U.S))
RR_ period 3 <- data.frame(RR3Mode=exp(TimePeriod3+S3.S+U.S))
RR_ period 4 <- data.frame(RR4Mode=exp(U.S))

where 

U.S<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.random$RegionID[,"mode"]

S1.S<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.random$RegionID1[,"mode"]

S2.S<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.random$RegionID2[,"mode"]

S3.S<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.random$RegionID3[,"mode"]

TimePeriod1<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.fixed["TP1999-2003","mode"]

TimePeriod2<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.fixed["TP2004-08","mode"]

TimePeriod3<-model.INLA.Lung.ON.SM.TN$summary.fixed["TP2009-13","mode"]


Now we need to find probability that RR_period1  to  RR_period4 are greater than 1. I saw in the e-book you recommeneded using

sapply(res$marginals.fitted.values, FUN = function(marg){1-inla.pmarginal(1, marginal = marg)})
 

but I am afraid that  marginals.fitted.values in our model are exactly equivalent to  RR_period1  to  RR_period4 or not?! Appreciate you to let us know how these marginals.fitted.values got calculated when we have 4 sets of random effects in the model. 

Thanks,

Shabnam Balamchi , PhD

Decision Scientist, Data and Decision Sciences

Hi Havard,

Thanks for your response. I wanted to add model object here but it is too large too be attached here. Can I have any email address to send it through outlook or gmail?

The code that I am currently using to generate PPs is:

################

### RR

U.S<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.random$RegionID[,"mean"]
areanum=length(U.S)


S1.S<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.random$RegionID1[,"mean"]
length(S1.S)
S2.S<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.random$RegionID2[,"mean"]
length(S2.S)
S3.S<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.random$RegionID3[,"mean"]
length(S3.S)



TimePeriod1<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.fixed["TP1999-2003","mean"]
length(TimePeriod1)
TimePeriod2<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.fixed["TP2004-2008","mean"]
length(TimePeriod2)
TimePeriod3<-model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$summary.fixed["TP2009-2013","mean"]
length(TimePeriod3)


#COV.FE<-SmK+depr2.U+depr3.U+depr4.U+depr5.U+dep2.U+dep3.U+dep4.U+dep5.U+ins2.U+ins3.U+ins4.U+ins5.U



################# RR (Rate ratios) adjusted for covariates
RR_adj1<- data.frame(RR1mean=exp(TimePeriod1+S1.S+U.S))
RR_adj2<- data.frame(RR2mean=exp(TimePeriod2+S2.S+U.S))
RR_adj3<- data.frame(RR3mean=exp(TimePeriod3+S3.S+U.S))
RR_adj4<- data.frame(RR4mean=exp(U.S))

######PPs

PP1=matrix(NA,areanum,1)
for(i in 1:areanum){
A<-inla.rmarginal(100000,model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.fixed$`TP1999-2003`+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID1[[i]]+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID[[i]])
PP1[i]<-mean(exp(A)>1.0)
}

PP_adj1=data.frame(PP1=PP1)

PP2=matrix(NA,areanum,1)
for(i in 1:areanum){
  A<-inla.rmarginal(100000,model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.fixed$`TP2004-2008`+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID2[[i]]+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID[[i]])
  PP2[i]<-mean(exp(A)>1.0)
}

PP_adj2=data.frame(PP2=PP2)

PP3=matrix(NA,areanum,1)
for(i in 1:areanum){
  A<-inla.rmarginal(100000,model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.fixed$`TP2009-2013`+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID3[[i]]+model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID[[i]])
  PP3[i]<-mean(exp(A)>1.0)
}


PP_adj3=data.frame(PP3=PP3)

PP4=matrix(NA,areanum,1)
for(i in 1:areanum){
  A<-inla.rmarginal(100000,model.INLA.Cx.ON.SM$marginals.random$RegionID[[i]])
  PP4[i]<-mean(exp(A)>1.0)
}

PP_adj4=data.frame(PP4=PP4)


However, PPs are mostly around 50% which is not correct for sure. This approach works for MCMC but not for INLA I guess.


Thanks,
Shabnam
